text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said his government would quit if parliament pushed through a bill on local government financing that wpould harm Portugal's chances of joining the European single currency.
- According to an opinion poll, the ruling Socialist Party has the support of 39.5 percent of Portuguese voters, 1.5 percentage points more than the opposition centre-right Social Democratic Party.
- Debts of Portuguese families stood at 30.7 percent of GDP in 1996, compared with 16 percent in 1991, the Bank of Portugal said on its annual report for 1996.
- Real estate company Grao Para and the government have reached an agreement under which a state company will manage Estoril motor racing circuit near Lisbon.

Portuguese banking groups Banco Comercial Portugues and Banco Portugues de Investimento hold about 11 percent of the capital of cement group Cimpor, Cimpor president Antonio Sousa Gomes told the paper.

- The governor of the Bank of Portugal, Antonio de Sousa, said the Portuguese economy was growing briskly and that the Bank of Portugal may revise its forecast for 1997 GDP growth upwards towards the upper limit of a range between 3.00 and 3.75 percent.
